subject: Energy
title: Flywheel Energy Storage
description: A micro-lesson that makes Flywheel Energy Storage usable.

hook.text: Flywheels store energy as rotational kinetic energy—a heavy disc spins at thousands of RPM in a vacuum chamber.

buildup.text: To store energy, a motor spins the flywheel faster. To release it, the spinning flywheel drives a generator.

discovery.text: Response time is nearly instantaneous—flywheels can absorb or deliver full power in milliseconds.

twist.text: Flywheels lose energy to friction continuously—even with magnetic bearings in vacuum, they drain within hours.

climax.text: They're ideal for short bursts—frequency regulation, UPS systems, and smoothing rapid renewable fluctuations.

punchline.text: Spin fast, deliver instantly—flywheels are energy on demand.

quiz.question: What is a flywheel's main limitation?
options: Energy drains within hours due to friction
